# UPD-005: Release is within standard support

- **Group:** Updates
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

After a release leaves standard support it gets no security fixes from the distribution (Ubuntu Pro or Debian LTS aside), so every new bug stays open. The check uses an embedded table of end of support dates; a release missing from it is reported unknown.

## Verify by hand

```sh
cat /etc/os-release
```

## How to fix it

Upgrade to a supported release (do-release-upgrade on Ubuntu, the Debian release notes upgrade procedure).

## What a fix can break

A release upgrade is a major change: test it on a copy and keep a backup and console access.

Run `stackward explain UPD-005` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
